title: Deterministic eligible-provider routing
instruction: Write solution.py defining solve(value). The input is a JSON object with max_latency_ms and providers. Return the chosen provider's name as a string, or null if none qualify. max_latency_ms must be a finite nonnegative JSON number (a boolean is not a number for this contract); providers must be a list. Return null if either requirement is not met or either field is absent. A provider qualifies only if it is an object, eligible is the JSON boolean true, name is a nonempty string, and price and latency_ms are finite nonnegative JSON numbers (not booleans). Its latency_ms must be at or below max_latency_ms. Skip malformed or ineligible entries. Among qualifying providers choose the lowest price; break price ties using the lexicographically smallest name with Python string ordering, case-sensitive, without trimming or normalization. Provider order must not affect the result. Equal names produce the same returned string, so duplicate names require no extra tie-break. Do not mutate the input or use network calls. This exercise routes supplied synthetic observations; it does not measure real latency, model quality, or provider availability. Use only Python's standard library.
